Useful for questions about the company's business lines, its Q3 2026 revenue and growth, or its return to profitability. The section is text only and contains no tables or images.
children.text: Nimbus Robotics is a fictional maker of warehouse robots and delivery drones. In the third quarter of 2026, revenue grew 12 percent on the same quarter last year to 41.4 million dollars, and the company returned to operating profit.

children.title: Financial Results
children.summary: Covers quarterly financial performance: revenue by region (North America 18.4M, Europe 11.2M, Asia-Pacific 9.7M, Other 2.1M, total 41.4M USD millions), operating costs by category (manufacturing, R&D, sales and marketing, G&A, total 37.4M), and operating income of 4.0M versus a 1.2M loss a year earlier. Also reports cash and equivalents of 52.6M, up from 47.9M last quarter, with no outstanding debt. Tables show the regional revenue breakdown and the operating cost breakdown. Answers questions about revenue by region, cost structure, profitability, and cash position.
children.text:
Revenue by region
North America remains the largest market, followed by Europe. Asia-Pacific grew fastest.

| Region | Revenue (USD millions) |
| --- | --- |
| North America | 18.4 |
| Europe | 11.2 |
| Asia-Pacific | 9.7 |
| Other | 2.1 |
| Total | 41.4 |

Operating costs
| Category | Cost (USD millions) |
| --- | --- |
| Manufacturing | 17.3 |
| Research and development | 9.8 |
| Sales and marketing | 6.4 |
| General and administrative | 3.9 |
| Total | 37.4 |

Operating income for the quarter was 4.0 million dollars, compared with a loss of 1.2 million dollars a year ago.

Cash position
Cash and equivalents ended the quarter at 52.6 million dollars, up from 47.9 million at the end of the previous quarter. The company has no outstanding debt.

children.title: Product Updates
children.summary: Covers two product milestones: the WR-4 warehouse robot, which began shipping in July with 310 quarterly orders (mostly existing customers), and its specs of 60 kg payload and ten hours of runtime per charge. Also covers the D-2 delivery drone, which passed regulatory testing in two European countries and plans commercial deliveries starting in Q1 next year with pharmacy partners. Useful for questions about WR-4 specifications or sales, D-2 regulatory status, or launch timing. No tables or images.
children.text:
Warehouse robot WR-4
The WR-4 began shipping in July. It carries loads of up to 60 kilograms and runs for ten hours per charge. Orders for the quarter reached 310 units, mostly from existing customers.

Delivery drone D-2
The D-2 completed regulatory testing in two European countries. Commercial deliveries are planned to begin in the first quarter of next year, starting with pharmacy partners.

children.title: Risks and Outlook
children.summary: Covers the company's main risks and its Q4 guidance. Supply risk centers on battery cells, which come from two suppliers, with a third being qualified to reduce shortage risk. Regulatory risk comes from country-specific drone rules, and possible flight-altitude limit changes could delay the D-2 launch in some markets. It also gives Q4 guidance of 44 to 47 million dollars in revenue and continued operating-level profitability. Use it to answer questions about supply chain, regulatory, or Q4 outlook; there are no tables or images.
children.text:
Supply chain
Battery cells remain the main supply risk. Nimbus buys from two suppliers and is qualifying a third to lower the chance of a shortage.

Regulation
Drone rules differ by country, and a change to flight-altitude limits could delay the D-2 launch in some markets.

Guidance for Q4
The company expects Q4 revenue between 44 and 47 million dollars and expects to stay profitable at the operating level.
